title: Medical and Life-Support Protections: Holdings across Service Agreements and One Open Certification per Agreement
content:
**Rule.** Under Medical and Life-Support Protections, a customer may hold medical protections on more than one service agreement only where a patient lives full time at each address. No other certification on the same service agreement is in pending certification or active status. A customer moving from a certificate to an allowance or a life-support registration withdraws the first before applying for the second.

## The condition on a new application

Applications are accepted only where no other certification on the same service agreement is in pending certification or active status. The test is made against the company's own certification records for the service agreement named in the application, before the application is accepted; what the customer says about the agreement's existing certifications does not replace the record. Each application is its own record, distinguished by its application date.

| Other certification on the same service agreement | Effect on the new application |
|---|---|
| in pending certification status | not accepted |
| in active status | not accepted |
| denied, expired or withdrawn | does not engage this condition |
| none | does not engage this condition |

Only certifications on the **same** service agreement are counted. A certification held on another of the customer's agreements does not engage this condition; holdings on several agreements are governed by the full-time residence condition in the rule above.

## Several agreements

There is no fixed numerical limit on the number of service agreements on which one customer may hold medical protections. The limit is the residence condition: each address must be one where a patient lives full time.

## Moving from a certificate to an allowance or a life-support registration

A customer moving from a certificate to an allowance or a life-support registration withdraws the first before applying for the second. While the certificate remains pending or active on the agreement, the condition in the table above is engaged for the new application on that agreement.

### Hypothetical cases

1. A customer's agreement carries a Standard Medical Baseline Allowance in active status, and the customer applies on that same agreement for a Life-Support Registration. Another certification on the same agreement is active: the application is not accepted.
2. A customer's agreement carries a Combined Medical Baseline Allowance whose status is expired. An application on that agreement is not stopped by this condition, since an expired certification is neither pending nor active.
3. A customer holds a Medical Emergency Certificate on the agreement at a home where the patient lives full time, and applies for a Medical Emergency Certificate on a second agreement at an address where another patient lives full time. Each address has a full-time patient, and the second agreement has no other pending or active certification, so neither part of this rule stands in the way.
